quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help reduce your chance of a crash?

options.text: Be visible by wearing proper clothing and using your headlight.
Signal your intentions using turn signals and brake lights.
Look for hazards in your path.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible to other drivers, signal your intentions, and keep space around you. Look for hazards and be ready to react. Hoping other drivers see you is not a safety strategy.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Move to one side of your lane to share it with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow them to pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make things more dangerous by causing them to tailgate you at higher speed.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before starting the motorcycle
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before you start your motorcycle. Position them so you can see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you.

questions.question: You should use more space between you and other vehicles when:
questions.correctAnswerText: Roads are slippery.
questions.explanation: A two-second following distance is normal. Use more space when conditions make it harder to stop, such as on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: Why should you wear riding gloves?

options.text: You should not wear them because they make your hands too hot.
They give you a better grip on the handgrips.
You should not wear them because they make controls harder to operate.
Wear them only on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give you a better grip on the handgrips.
questions.explanation: Wear gloves made of leather or other durable material when riding. They improve your grip on the handgrips and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: If a dog chases your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the animal to lose interest.
Slow down as you approach it, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach it, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, downshift and slow down as you approach it. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is how many times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Five times
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

questions.question: As a beginning rider following another vehicle, what distance should you maintain?

options.text: Get as close as possible to the other vehicle.
Do not worry about your following distance.
Always ride in the left part of the lane so the driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: A minimum four-second distance.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should maintain at least a four-second following distance. Increase this distance whenever conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: To lean your motorcycle for a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handgrip opposite the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. To make it lean, push on the handgrip in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: When riding near stopped or slow-moving cars, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Pull over and wait until traffic starts moving.
Ride on the shoulder to get through quickly.
Weave between cars to get through quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not weave between cars.
questions.explanation: Riding between slow or parked cars can expose you to hazards like opening doors or cars pulling into traffic. If a hazard appears, you will not have room to maneuver safely. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers do not expect to see you there.

questions.question: Where do most crashes happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles. These happen just a few minutes after you start riding.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of crashing?

options.text: Do not use turn signals when changing lanes.
Look only five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to others. Use turn signals, your brake light, and good lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle. Look ahead, behind, and to the sides. Always be ready to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: How should you sit to control a motorcycle properly?

options.text: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
Sit far enough back so you can keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to help with balance.

questions.question: What happens if you shift into a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and a warning light will appear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you go too fast when shifting into a lower gear, your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid. This causes you to lose control. Slow down before shifting into a lower gear.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: Brakes in both the front and rear.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes in both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes. One controls the front wheel and one controls the rear wheel.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects the eyes and face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough protection.

questions.question: What is the best sitting position when riding?

options.text: You can easily reach the controls.
Your arms stay straight when holding the handgrips.
Your knees stay away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can steer with your arms, not hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips and you should not have to stretch to reach them. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.

questions.question: Which helmet type offers the most protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Full-face
questions.explanation: Helmets come in one-half, three-quarter, and full-face styles. A full-face helmet gives the best protection.

questions.question: How many times more likely are helmeted riders to survive a crash than those without helmets?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: At any speed, wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash than riding without a helmet.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to handle differently while riding?

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over and check the chain.
Pull over and check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A change in how your motorcycle handles may mean a tire has failed. If you notice a change in handling, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT need to be checked before every ride?
questions.correctAnswerText: The seat fabric
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle carefully. Check the rims and spokes for bending, looseness, or damage. Check your tire condition and tread. Check all your lights. You do not need to check the seat fabric.

questions.question: What is the best way to brake in a straight line to stop in the shortest distance?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel
Use both the front and rear brakes and lock the rear wheel

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel
questions.explanation: On a straight road, use both brakes to stop in the shortest distance. Do not lock either brake.

questions.question: There is often an oily strip in the center of a lane. Is it safe for motorcycles?

options.text: No, it is never safe for motorcycles
Yes, unless the road is wet
No, you should always avoid it

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, unless the road is wet
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of the lane. When the road is dry, this area has enough grip for motorcycles to ride safely. The strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can ride to one side and stay in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is following too closely
When there is a stop sign ahead
When your signals are not working

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is following too closely
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before you slow down if someone is following you too closely. The other driver may not notice the hazard ahead that is making you slow. Also flash your brake light when you are about to slow down in a place where drivers might not expect it.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when another vehicle is passing you?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding toward the passing vehicle increases the risk of a collision. Riding away from the passing vehicle may make the driver think they can re-enter your lane too soon.

questions.question: A small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid the animal
Switch lanes as quickly as possible
Flash your lights to scare the animal

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane
questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal, but if you are in traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving to miss an animal could cause you to hit another vehicle. A small animal is less dangerous than a collision with another car.

questions.question: How can you reduce the time you need to react to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and brakes
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your fingers near the clutch and both brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: How should you hold the handgrips when riding over rough surfaces?

options.text: Loosely to allow the motorcycle to move
Lightly and use lots of throttle

questions.correctAnswerText: Firmly to maintain control
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly when riding on rough surfaces. This keeps you in control of the motorcycle's direction.

questions.question: What is the rule for passing another vehicle?

options.text: You can complete a pass in a no passing zone
You can go 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass
You must start and complete the pass in a passing zone
You must complete the pass on the shoulder

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and complete the pass in a passing zone
questions.explanation: Pass only where it is safe and legal. Follow the speed limit and stay within passing zones.

questions.question: How should you approach a blind intersection?

options.text: Ride where other drivers will see you as early as possible
Always stay in the left lane
Slowly sneak up to the intersection
Weave in your lane so your headlight is more visible

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride where other drivers will see you as early as possible
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position yourself in the part of your lane where oncoming drivers will see you first. For example, if the blind corner is on your right, ride in the left part of your lane so drivers see you sooner.

questions.question: What color are warning signs and what color is the lettering?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When should you use your turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to speed up

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you change lanes
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists ride when entering a highway or curve?

options.text: One behind the other in a single line
On the far right side of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: One behind the other in a single line
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is normally good, but switch to single-file when turning, going around curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: What percent of motorcycle and car crashes happen because the car driver did not yield the right-of-way?
questions.correctAnswerText: More than 50 percent
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes happen because the car driver failed to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: What three things should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder
Look over your shoulder and change lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see if another vehicle is near you.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake on a motorcycle?

options.text: Every time you slow down or stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you slow down or stop
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does SIPDE stand for?

options.text: Stop, Increase, Pass, Downshift, and Enter
Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute
Side, Intercept, Plan, Demonstrate, and Exit
Slide, Impede, Position, Decode, and Extreme

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute
questions.explanation: SIPDE is a strategy experienced riders use to make safe decisions. It stands for Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute.

questions.question: How should your following distance at night compare to during the day?

options.text: Keep a longer distance at night
Keep a shorter distance at night
Keep the same distance all the time

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance at night
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see distances because there are fewer light and shadow clues. Keep a longer following distance at night than during the day.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces create poor traction. Wet pavement, gravel, mud, snow, ice, and metal road covers are all more slippery than dry pavement.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a slippery surface?

options.text: Oil in the middle of a lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, mud, snow, ice, and metal road covers are all slippery. Dry pavement is not slippery.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies some rear braking when you use the front brake.
Applies some front braking when you use the rear brake.
Applies equal braking to both front and rear when you use either brake.
Remembers how hard you usually brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies some front braking when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system is a type of linked braking system. It applies some front braking whenever you use the rear brake. Read your motorcycle's owner's manual for details about your specific braking system.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, why should you ride in the left portion of your lane?

options.text: It helps you see farther ahead.
It limits how far you can see.
It makes it hard to see past the other vehicle.
It lets the other driver speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see farther ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when you prepare to pass. This helps you see farther ahead and makes you more visible to other drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs show road rules, such as speed limits. They are usually white with black letters or symbols. You must follow all rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: What should a helmet do to give you the best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly on your head
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest
Slow down to approach the dog, then speed up and leave it behind

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to approach the dog, then speed up and leave it behind
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If a dog chases you, downshift and slow down as you approach it. Then accelerate and leave the dog behind.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week.

questions.question: What is true about a motorcycle with a sidecar?

options.text: It can tip over if you turn too fast
It can take corners at any speed
You should not put items in the sidecar

questions.correctAnswerText: It can tip over if you turn too fast
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels, a sidecar motorcycle can tip over if you turn too sharply or go too fast around a corner.

questions.question: You are planning to ride with 12 other riders. What should you do?

options.text: Invite more riders because riding is more fun in a larger group
Split into at least two smaller groups
Race to your destination as long as everyone knows where to meet

questions.correctAnswerText: Split into at least two smaller groups
questions.explanation: Groups with more than four or five riders should split into smaller groups. A large group can slow traffic. Riders may get separated and take unsafe risks trying to catch up.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol was consumed
How often a person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect blood alcohol content: how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Your sex, physical condition, and food intake may also have some effect.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of the lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: An oily or greasy strip
questions.explanation: Car drippings often form an oily strip down the center of each lane. When roads are dry, it is usually safe for motorcycles to ride on this center strip.
